q: How many books are in the Bible?
why: 39 in the Old Testament, 27 in the New.

q: Who was thrown into the lions’ den?
why: Daniel, for praying when a new law forbade it.

q: What did God create on the first day?
why: Light — the sun does not appear until day four.

q: Who baptised Jesus?
why: John, in the River Jordan.

q: How many disciples did Jesus choose?
why: Twelve — one for each tribe of Israel.

q: What did David use against Goliath?
why: A sling and five smooth stones, having refused Saul’s armour.

q: Who was swallowed by a great fish?
why: Jonah, running from God’s call to Nineveh.

q: Which book opens the New Testament?
why: Matthew — though Mark was probably written first.

q: Who denied Jesus three times?
why: Peter, before the rooster crowed — and Jesus restored him afterwards.

q: Which queen risked her life for her people?
why: Esther — ‘if I perish, I perish’.

q: What is the first commandment Jesus called greatest?
why: Love God with all your heart, soul, mind and strength.

q: How long was Jesus in the tomb?
why: Three days, counted inclusively — part of Friday, Saturday, part of Sunday.

q: Who wrote most of the New Testament letters?
why: Paul — thirteen letters carry his name.

q: What does ‘gospel’ mean?
why: It translates a word for good news, used in the Roman world for imperial announcements.

q: Which city did Jonah refuse to go to?
why: Nineveh, the capital of the empire that terrorised Israel.

q: What happened at Pentecost?
why: The Spirit came and the gospel was heard in every language present.

q: What did Moses stretch his hand over so it parted?
why: Israel walked through on dry ground — Exodus 14.

q: What did God send to feed Israel in the desert?
why: It appeared with the morning dew — Exodus 16.

q: How many plagues struck Egypt?
why: The last one was the reason for the Passover.

q: Who was sold by his brothers and ended up in Egypt?
why: Years later he fed the same brothers in a famine.

q: Whose walls fell down after Israel marched around them?
why: Seven days of marching, then a shout — Joshua 6.

q: Which strong man lost his strength when his hair was cut?
why: His strength was never really in the hair — it was in the vow it stood for.

q: Who said “Where you go, I will go”?
why: Ruth said it to Naomi, her mother-in-law, not to a husband.

q: Who was the first king of Israel?
why: The people asked for a king so they could be like the nations around them.

q: Which king asked God for wisdom instead of riches?
why: He got the wisdom, and the riches as well — 1 Kings 3.

q: Who was taken up to heaven in a whirlwind?
why: Elisha watched it happen and picked up his cloak.

q: Who were the three men thrown into the fiery furnace?
why: They said God could rescue them — “but if not”, they still would not bow.

q: What was Jacob’s name changed to?
why: It happened the night he wrestled until daybreak.

q: How many sons did Jacob have?
why: The twelve tribes of Israel are named after them.

q: What did God give Moses on Mount Sinai?
why: Written on two tablets of stone.

q: Who led Israel into the promised land after Moses died?
why: “Be strong and courageous” was said to him.

q: Which boy heard God calling him at night in the temple?
why: He kept thinking it was Eli — 1 Samuel 3.

q: What did the Israelites make while Moses was up the mountain?
why: Aaron made it out of their own jewellery.

q: Who rebuilt the wall of Jerusalem?
why: It took fifty-two days, with opposition the whole way.

q: Who lost everything and still would not curse God?
why: His friends had a lot of explanations, and God said they were wrong.

q: What did Abraham almost sacrifice on the mountain?
why: God stopped him and provided a ram instead.

q: Where was Jesus born?
why: In Bethlehem, though he grew up in Nazareth.

q: What was Jesus’ first recorded miracle?
why: At a wedding in Cana, because they had run out — John 2.

q: How many loaves fed the five thousand?
why: Five loaves and two fish, and twelve baskets left over.

q: Which disciple walked on the water towards Jesus?
why: He started to sink when he looked at the wind instead.

q: Who was made to carry Jesus’ cross?
why: A stranger pulled out of the crowd — Mark 15:21.

q: Who was the first to see Jesus alive again?
why: She thought he was the gardener at first.

q: What came on the disciples at Pentecost?
why: Like wind and fire, and they spoke in other languages — Acts 2.

q: Who was blinded by a light on the road to Damascus?
why: He was on his way to arrest Christians when it happened.

q: What was Matthew’s job before he followed Jesus?
why: A job that made him a traitor to most of his neighbours.

q: Who climbed a tree to see Jesus?
why: He was short, rich, and hated — and Jesus went to his house.

q: In the parable, what did the father do when his lost son came home?
why: He ran — which grown men of that time did not do.

q: Who stopped to help the wounded man on the road?
why: The one the listeners would have least expected.

q: Where did Jesus pray the night he was arrested?
why: “Not my will, but yours be done.”

q: Which disciple said he would not believe until he saw the wounds?
why: Jesus showed him, and he said “My Lord and my God.”

q: Whom did Jesus raise after four days in the tomb?
why: Jesus wept before he did it — John 11.

q: What did Jesus say to the storm on the lake?
why: And it went completely calm, which frightened them more than the storm.

q: Who was the Roman governor who handed Jesus over?
why: He washed his hands, which changed nothing.

q: What is the first book of the Bible?
why: Genesis means “beginning”.

q: What is the last book of the Bible?
why: Written by John while he was exiled.

q: Which book comes straight after Genesis?
why: Exodus — the way out of Egypt.

q: How many books are in the Old Testament?
why: 39 in the Old, 27 in the New, 66 altogether.

q: How many books are in the New Testament?
why: Four Gospels, Acts, the letters, and Revelation.

q: Which book of the Bible has the most chapters?
why: 150 of them, written by several people over centuries.

q: What are the first four books of the New Testament called?
why: Matthew, Mark, Luke and John — four accounts of one life.

q: Which psalm begins “Yahweh is my shepherd”?
why: Written by David, who had actually been a shepherd.

q: Which book tells the story of the first church?
why: It starts at Pentecost and never really ends.

q: Which Gospel begins “In the beginning was the Word”?
why: John starts before the manger, at creation.

q: What did Jesus say to do to your enemies?
why: “Love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you.”

q: How does the Lord’s Prayer begin?
why: Jesus taught his disciples to start with “Father”.

q: Jesus said “I am the good ___”.
why: The shepherd who does not run when the wolf comes — John 10.

q: Jesus said “I am the way, the truth and the ___”.
why: John 14:6, said to disciples who were frightened about the future.

q: Who did Jesus say is greatest in the kingdom of heaven?
why: He put a child in front of them to make the point.

q: How many times did Jesus say to forgive?
why: Peter offered seven and thought he was being generous.

q: What does grace mean?
why: If it could be earned it would be wages, not a gift.

q: What did Jesus tell the disciples to do at the end of Matthew?
why: The Great Commission — Matthew 28:19.

q: How many fruits of the Spirit does Paul list?
why: Love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness, self-control.

q: Which letter contains the chapter about love read at weddings?
why: Chapter 13 — written to a church that was arguing badly.

q: What was Paul’s trade?
why: He worked while he preached, so as not to be a burden — Acts 18:3.

q: Who travelled with Paul on his first journey?
why: Barnabas, whose name means “son of encouragement”.

q: Which prophet saw a valley full of dry bones?
why: God asked him whether the bones could live, and he said “you know”.

q: Which prophet said “I am only a child” when God called him?
why: God told him to go anyway — Jeremiah 1:6.

q: Which prophet saw the Lord high and lifted up in the temple?
why: “Here I am. Send me!” — Isaiah 6.

q: What did Daniel refuse to stop doing, even when it was illegal?
why: Three times a day, with his windows open.

q: What does the name “Immanuel” mean?
why: Isaiah said it first; Matthew applied it to Jesus.

q: Which prophet married Gomer, as a picture of God and Israel?
why: The marriage itself was the message.

q: Who was the high priest at Jesus’ trial?
why: Caiaphas presided; Annas, his father-in-law, questioned Jesus first.

q: Which island was John on when he saw the revelation?
why: He had been exiled there — Revelation 1:9.

q: Who was chosen to replace Judas among the twelve?
why: Chosen by lot, then never mentioned again — Acts 1:26.

q: Who does Paul name as raising Timothy in the faith?
options: His grandmother Lois and mother Eunice
why: 2 Timothy 1:5 — a faith handed down through two women.

q: What happened to the temple curtain when Jesus died?
why: From top to bottom — the way in was open.

q: Which mountain did Elijah run to, where he heard a still small voice?
why: Not in the wind, the earthquake or the fire — 1 Kings 19.

q: What did Elijah call down on Mount Carmel?
why: After soaking the altar in water first.

q: Who was king of Judah when Jerusalem fell to Babylon?
why: The last king before the exile — 2 Kings 25.

q: What did Jesus do with bread and wine at the Last Supper?
options: Called them his body and blood
why: “Do this in memory of me.”

q: Which two brothers left their nets to follow Jesus first?
why: “Come after me, and I will make you fishers for men.”

q: Which shortest verse in most English Bibles is two words long?
why: John 11:35, at the tomb of his friend.

q: What language was most of the Old Testament written in?
why: With a few passages in Aramaic.

q: What language was the New Testament written in?
why: Common Greek — the everyday language of the eastern empire.

q: What did the wise men bring Jesus?
why: Three gifts, though the Bible never says how many wise men.

q: Who hid the baby Moses in a basket?
why: His sister Miriam watched from the reeds, and Pharaoh’s daughter found him.

q: Who was Moses’ brother and spokesman?
why: Moses said he could not speak well, so Aaron spoke for him.

q: What sign did God give Noah after the flood?
why: A promise attached to something everybody can see.

q: In which town did Jesus grow up?
why: Nazareth, in Galilee — a place people made jokes about.

q: Who were Jesus' mother and the man who raised him?
why: Mary, and Joseph the carpenter.

q: Who came to see the newborn Jesus first?
why: Shepherds — the people nobody sent messages to.

q: Why did Mary lay Jesus in a manger?
options: There was no room in the inn
why: A manger is the box animals eat from. That was his first bed.

q: Where did Joseph take Mary and Jesus to escape Herod?
why: Egypt — Jesus was a refugee before he could walk.

q: What was Jesus doing when his parents lost him at twelve?
options: Sitting with the teachers in the temple
why: Asking questions, and answering them. He said he had to be in his Father's house.

q: What job did Jesus do before he began teaching?
why: He worked with his hands, like Joseph.

q: What happened when Jesus was baptised?
options: The Spirit came down like a dove and God spoke
why: “This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased.”

q: How long was Jesus tempted in the wilderness?
why: Forty days without food, and three temptations at the end of it.

q: How did Jesus answer every temptation in the wilderness?
why: “It is written…” — every single time.

q: What were Peter, Andrew, James and John doing when Jesus called them?
why: He said he would make them fishers of people.

q: What did Jesus call the twelve he chose?
why: Apostle means 'one who is sent'.

q: On what did Jesus preach the sermon with the Beatitudes?
why: The Sermon on the Mount, in Matthew 5 to 7.

q: How does each Beatitude begin?
why: Blessed are the poor in spirit, those who mourn, the meek…

q: Jesus said, “You are the salt of the earth, and the ___ of the world.”
why: A city on a hill cannot be hidden.

q: What did Jesus tell people to do about worrying?
options: Look at the birds — your Father feeds them
why: Matthew 6. Today has enough trouble of its own.

q: What did Jesus say to do when someone hurts you?
why: Seventy times seven, he said — which means stop counting.

q: How many people did Jesus feed with five loaves and two fish?
options: Five thousand men, plus women and children
why: And twelve baskets were left over.

q: What did Jesus do that made Peter step out of the boat?
why: Peter walked too — until he looked at the waves.

q: Whom did Jesus meet at the well in Samaria?
why: He offered her living water, and she told her whole town.

q: What did Jesus say to Martha before raising her brother?
options: I am the resurrection and the life
why: Then he wept with her, and then he called Lazarus out.

q: On the mountain of the transfiguration, who appeared with Jesus?
why: The law and the prophets, standing with the one they pointed to.

q: What did Jesus say when the disciples stopped children coming to him?
options: Let the little children come to me
why: And he said the kingdom belongs to people like them.

q: Who did Jesus say we should love as ourselves?
why: And then he told a story about who counts as a neighbour.

q: Jesus said, “I am the bread of ___.”
why: One of seven “I am” sayings in John's gospel.

q: How did Jesus enter Jerusalem on Palm Sunday?
why: A king came in peace, and the crowd waved palm branches.

q: What did Jesus do in the temple that made the leaders furious?
options: Turned over the money changers' tables
why: “My house shall be a house of prayer.”

q: What did Jesus do for his disciples at the Last Supper, before the meal?
why: The job of the lowest servant in the house.

q: Who betrayed Jesus, and with what?
why: For thirty pieces of silver.

q: What was written on the sign above Jesus on the cross?
why: Pilate meant it as a charge. It was true.

q: What did Jesus say about the people crucifying him?
why: “…for they do not know what they are doing.”

q: What did Jesus say to the criminal beside him on the cross?
options: It is too late for you
Today you will be with me in paradise
why: One sentence, at the very last minute. It was enough.

q: Who came to the tomb early on Sunday morning?
why: The first witnesses of the resurrection were women.

q: What did the angel say at the empty tomb?
options: He is not here — he has risen
why: “Why do you look for the living among the dead?”

q: What did Jesus cook for the disciples by the lake after he rose?
why: And then he asked Peter three times if he loved him.

q: What did Jesus tell Peter to do, three times, by the lake?
why: Three denials, three restorations. Peter was not finished.

q: What happened forty days after the resurrection?
why: The ascension. Two angels asked why they were still staring up.

q: Why does John say he wrote his gospel?
options: So that you may believe and have life
why: John 20:31. He picked seven signs and said that was enough.

q: What did Jesus mean by calling himself the Son of Man?
options: He was claiming the figure from Daniel 7
why: It sounds humble. Anyone who knew Daniel heard a throne.

q: Whom did Jesus ask, “Who do you say that I am?”
why: Peter answered: “You are the Christ, the Son of the living God.”

q: Which sector is FLCC Abundance in?
why: Hope sector, with FB, F&T and Cornerstone.

q: Which country is our church family in?
why: FLCC serves Filipinos living and working in Kuwait.

q: FLCC is part of which wider network?
why: The National Evangelical Church in Kuwait — N.E.C.K. — is the church we belong to.

q: How many churches are in the FLCC BOTR network?
why: Fourteen, spread across Kuwait, all part of one family.

q: The 14 churches are grouped into three sectors. What are they named after?
why: Hope, Faith and Love — from 1 Corinthians 13:13.

q: Which verse gives the three sectors their names — Faith, Hope and Love?
why: “Now faith, hope and love remain — these three. The greatest of these is love.”

q: Who is the lead pastor of the FLCC BOTR network?
why: Rev. Jopet Alim leads the whole FLCC BOTR network.

q: How many people does FLCC hope to reach in 2026 alone?
why: 54,000 this year, on the way to 270,000 by 2030.

q: Where does the main N.E.C.K. service meet?
why: The National Evangelical Church in Kuwait, in Kuwait City.

q: What day does the main service meet?
why: Friday morning — the weekend here is Friday and Saturday.

q: How many people does FLCC hope to introduce to Jesus by 2030?
why: 270,000 — which is why every one of us is asked to go and tell someone.

q: Which church is in the Hope sector along with Abundance and Cornerstone?
why: Hope sector is Abundance, FB, F&T and Cornerstone.

q: Shekinah, Agape and HOTK belong to which sector?
why: Faith sector, along with BOTR Friday and BOTR Sunday.

q: Which sector is MTCC, GIL, JAOC and Harvester in?
why: Love sector — which also includes the Virtual Church.

q: One of the 14 FLCC churches has no building at all. Which?
why: The Virtual Church meets online, for people who cannot get to a building.

q: FLCC's vision says we are a family of what?
why: “A family of prayer and worshippers raised up from its own harvest.”

q: Our vision talks about two great things Jesus gave us. What are they?
options: The Great Wall and the Great Lake
The Great Feast and the Great Song
The Great Commandment and the Great Commission
why: Love God and love people; then go and make disciples.

q: What is the Great Commission?
options: Go and make disciples of all nations
why: Matthew 28:19 — the last thing Jesus told his friends to do.

q: What is the Great Commandment?
options: Love God, and love your neighbour
why: Jesus said everything else hangs on these two.

q: FLCC believes the Bible is what?
options: The inspired and authoritative Word of God
why: It is the first line of our statement of faith.

q: How many persons does our statement of faith say the one God exists in?
why: Father, Son and Holy Spirit — one God, three persons.

q: What does FLCC believe about how a person is saved?
why: Nobody earns it. It is a gift you receive.

q: How does FLCC baptise?
why: Water baptism by immersion, as Jesus was baptised.

q: Which two ordinances did the Lord set for the church?
options: Water baptism and the Lord's Supper
why: Baptism, once; the Lord's Supper, again and again.

q: What does our statement of faith say about Jesus' return?
options: Nobody can say anything about it
It is personal, and it could be soon
why: “Imminent and personal” — he is coming back himself.

q: Most FLCC members are far from the country they grew up in. Which country?
why: FLCC was founded to reach Filipinos working in Kuwait.

q: Ang FLCC ay itinatag upang akayin ang mga Pilipino sa Kuwait tungo saan?
why: To knowing Jesus — that is the whole purpose, in our own language.

q: Why does FLCC exist, in one line?
options: To lead people to Jesus and grow them in faith
why: Lead people to Jesus, grow them up in him, and send them out.

q: What is a satellite church?
options: A local church that is part of a bigger family
A church that only meets online
why: Each of the 14 FLCC churches is one, meeting near where its people live.

q: If you want to follow Jesus for the first time, who should you talk to?
options: A pastor, leader or your parents
why: Tell somebody. That is how the church has always worked.
